data.name: NE0001_Title
data.value: Declare one type per file with a matching file name

data.name: NE0001_MessageFormat
data.value: Type '{0}' should be declared in its own file named '{1}.cs'

data.name: NE0001_Description
data.value: Each top-level type should live in its own file whose name matches the type. Generic overloads are encoded by arity unless overload grouping is enabled.

data.name: NE0002_Title
data.value: Namespace should match the folder structure

data.name: NE0002_MessageFormat
data.value: Namespace '{0}' should be '{1}' to match the folder structure

data.name: NE0002_Description
data.value: Anchored at the RootNamespace MSBuild property, the declared namespace should equal RootNamespace joined with the file's folder path relative to the project directory, so the physical and logical layout stay aligned.

data.name: NE0003_Title
data.value: Declare a single namespace per file

data.name: NE0003_MessageFormat
data.value: Declare exactly one namespace per file

data.name: NE0003_Description
data.value: A file that declares more than one namespace (sibling or nested) hides types from the name-to-location mapping the other organization rules establish. Declare exactly one namespace per file.

data.name: NE0004_Title
data.value: Use the 'is null' pattern instead of '== null'

data.name: NE0004_MessageFormat
data.value: Use the 'is null' pattern instead of comparing with '== null'

data.name: NE0004_Description
data.value: A null comparison with the equality operator can be redefined by a user-defined 'operator =='; the 'is null' pattern always performs a null check and cannot be overridden, so it expresses the intent unambiguously.

data.name: NE0005_Title
data.value: Use the 'is not null' pattern instead of '!= null'

data.name: NE0005_MessageFormat
data.value: Use the 'is not null' pattern instead of comparing with '!= null'

data.name: NE0005_Description
data.value: A null comparison with the inequality operator can be redefined by a user-defined 'operator !='; the 'is not null' pattern always performs a null check and cannot be overridden, so it expresses the intent unambiguously.

data.name: NE0006_Title
data.value: Use the 'is not null' pattern instead of 'is object'

data.name: NE0006_MessageFormat
data.value: Use the 'is not null' pattern instead of 'is object' for a null check

data.name: NE0006_Description
data.value: Using 'is object' as a non-null check is easily misread as a type check; the 'is not null' pattern states the null check directly.

data.name: NE0007_Title
data.value: Use instead of ... or ... for C# keywords

data.name: NE0007_MessageFormat
data.value: Use <see langword="{0}"/> instead of <{1}>{0}</{1}>

data.name: NE0007_Description
data.value: A <c> or <code> element whose entire content is a single C# keyword (e.g. 'true', 'false', 'null') carries no semantic meaning; <see langword="..."/> is the dedicated construct for referencing a language keyword and is what IntelliSense and documentation generators recognize as such.

data.name: NE0008_Title
data.value: Use instead of ... or ... for native type names

data.name: NE0008_MessageFormat
data.value: Use <see cref="{0}"/> instead of <{1}>{0}</{1}>

data.name: NE0008_Description
data.value: A <c> or <code> element whose entire content is a single native type name (e.g. 'string', 'int') carries no semantic meaning; <see cref="..."/> is the dedicated construct for referencing a type and is what IntelliSense and documentation generators recognize as such.

data.name: NE0009_Title
data.value: Check for cancellation at the start of the method body

data.name: NE0009_MessageFormat
data.value: Method '{0}' has a CancellationToken parameter but does not check for cancellation at the start of its body

data.name: NE0009_Description
data.value: A method accepting a CancellationToken should honor it as early as possible. As the first statement after any leading guard clauses, call 'token.ThrowIfCancellationRequested()' or check 'token.IsCancellationRequested' and return, so cancellation is observed before any other work runs.

data.name: NE0010_Title
data.value: Accept a CancellationToken parameter on an asynchronous method

data.name: NE0010_MessageFormat
data.value: Method '{0}' returns {1} and should accept a CancellationToken parameter

data.name: NE0010_Description
data.value: A method returning Task, Task<T>, ValueTask, ValueTask<T>, or IAsyncEnumerable<T> represents an operation a caller may want to cancel; accepting a CancellationToken parameter lets callers request cancellation and lets the method propagate it to the operations it awaits or yields from.

data.name: NE0011_Title
data.value: Avoid #region directives

data.name: NE0011_MessageFormat
data.value: Avoid using '#region' directives

data.name: NE0011_Description
data.value: #region directives encourage hiding code instead of decomposing it into smaller, well-named members or types. A #region nested inside a member body is reported as a warning; one wrapping type-, namespace-, or file-level content (whole classes, using directives, …) is reported as a suggestion.

data.name: NE0012_Title
data.value: Use an explicit numeric literal suffix

data.name: NE0012_MessageFormat
data.value: Numeric literal '{0}' should be '{1}'

data.name: NE0012_Description
data.value: A numeric literal converted to long, ulong, uint, float, double, or decimal should carry that type's canonical, upper-case suffix (L, UL, U, F, D, M) instead of relying on an implicit conversion, so the type is explicit at the literal itself. A hexadecimal or binary integer literal converted to float, double, or decimal is left alone, since that format has no such suffix to add.

data.name: NE0013_Title
data.value: Use a numeric literal suffix instead of casting the literal

data.name: NE0013_MessageFormat
data.value: Cast '{0}' should be the literal '{1}'

data.name: NE0013_Description
data.value: An integer literal immediately cast to long, ulong, uint, float, double, or decimal (e.g. '(long)0') should use that type's literal suffix instead ('0L'), which says the same thing without the cast. Only a plain integer literal (no existing suffix, no decimal point or exponent) is rewritten, since rewriting a literal that already has a fractional part could change its value.
